base34.name: Base game
base34.story: The advanced setup: hexes and tokens are placed at random.
rules: The robber starts on the desert; no number token goes there.
Assemble the sea frame from its six pieces in any order, harbor symbols facing out.
Founding: the first round goes clockwise, the second counter-clockwise; your second settlement pays starting resources at once.
With three players, put the white pieces back in the box.

base56.name: Base game
base56.story: The 5–6 player extension: more hexes, tokens and harbors, and a second desert.
rules: Two deserts: the robber starts on either of them.
After each player’s turn comes a special building phase.
The frame’s outline here is approximate; the hex and token counts are the standard ones.

s1.name: Heading for New Shores
s1.story: A main island and an archipelago of small isles; gold has been found on some of them.

rules: Your first 2 settlements go on the main island only; instead of a road on the coast you may place a ship at once.
Your first settlement on each small island earns 2 victory point tokens, so it is worth 3 VP.
The robber starts on the hills hex with the 12, the pirate on the sea hex marked X.
A gold field gives a settlement 1 resource card of its choice, a city 2.

Your first settlement on each small island earns 2 victory point tokens, so it is worth 3 VP.
The robber starts in the desert, the pirate on the sea hex marked X.
The hexes of the main island and of the small isles are placed at random; red numbers must not touch.

s2.name: The Four Islands
s2.story: An archipelago of four islands: every seafarer wants a foothold on all of them.

rules: Your first 2 settlements may go on one island or on two; those become your home islands.
Your first settlement on each foreign island earns 2 victory point tokens, 3 VP in all.
The robber starts on the hex with the 12, the pirate on the sea hex marked X.
Make sure forest and pasture don’t get only poor numbers: 2, 3, 11 and 12.
Your first 2 settlements may go on one island or on two; those become your home islands.
Your first settlement on each foreign island earns 2 victory point tokens, 3 VP in all.
The robber starts on the hex with the 12, the pirate on the sea hex marked X.
The outlines of the islands stay fixed; the hexes and tokens within an island may change.

s3.name: The Fog Islands
s3.story: Two islands, and between them a sea under thick fog.

rules: Fog hexes lie face down. When a road or ship reaches a corner of a hidden hex, the hex is turned over.
Land under the fog takes the top token of the face-down pile, and whoever revealed it takes 1 card of its resource. Sea gives nothing.
The robber starts on the hex with the 12, the pirate on the sea hex marked X.
No special victory points. These rules allow two red numbers side by side: switch off “6 and 8 never adjacent” in Setup to play it that way.
Fog hexes lie face down and are turned over when a road or ship reaches one of their corners.
Revealed land takes the top token of the pile and gives 1 card of its resource. Revealed sea gives nothing.
The robber starts on the hex with the 12, the pirate on the sea hex marked X.
This scenario has no special victory points.

s4.name: Through the Desert
s4.story: A desert cuts the main island in two, and small islands lie to the east.

rules: During founding, settle only on the larger part of the main island, on your side of the desert.
The small islands and the land beyond the desert are foreign: your first settlement there earns 2 extra VP.
Deserts get no tokens. The robber starts on any desert hex, the pirate on the sea hex marked X.
Red numbers may not touch each other or lie on gold fields.
During founding, settle only on the larger part of the main island, on your side of the desert.
The small islands and the land beyond the desert are foreign: your first settlement there earns 2 extra VP.
Deserts get no tokens. The robber starts on any desert hex, the pirate on the sea hex marked X.
Red numbers may not touch each other or lie on gold fields.

s5.name: The Forgotten Tribe
s5.tagline: An island and the tribe’s islets
s5.story: A long, narrow island, ringed by the inhabited islets of a forgotten tribe.
rules: The small islands have no number tokens, produce nothing and can’t be settled.
The tribe’s gifts lie on the routes by the islets: victory point tokens, development cards and free harbors go to whoever places or moves a ship there.
The robber starts on any desert; it may neither enter the small islands nor return to its starting hex.
Make sure the three outermost hexes of the main island don’t get the best numbers: 5, 6, 8 and 9.

s6.name: Cloth for Catan
s6.story: Two main islands, and between them villages that weave the finest cloth.
rules: Each small island gets 2 number tokens placed right on its corners: these are villages. Put 5 cloth tokens next to each village.
Reach a village with a line of ships and take 1 cloth at once, then 1 more each time its number is rolled.
2 cloth make 1 VP; a single cloth is worth nothing. The Longest Trade Route card isn’t used.
The game also ends when only 3 villages have cloth left: the player with the most VP wins.

s7.name: The Pirate Islands
s7.story: The eastern island is your home. Pirates hold the western islands, and they need an answer.
rules: Everyone starts on the eastern island: 1 settlement with a ship as the map shows, plus 2 normal settlements.
Three hexes on the western islands get no number token and produce nothing.
The pirate fleet sails clockwise around the central islands, as many hexes as the smaller die shows.
The Longest Trade Route and Largest Army cards aren’t used; knight cards turn ships into warships.

s8.name: The Wonders of Catan
s8.story: After the pirates’ defeat, great wonders rise on the northern islands.
rules: Your first 2 settlements go on the large island only.
Each player builds one of five wonders in 4 stages, paying 5 of the listed resources per stage.
Your first settlement on each small island earns 1 victory point token.
Hexes next to a desert must not get a 6 or an 8.

s9.name: New World
s9.story: A free scenario: every hex, the sea included, is placed at random.
rules: The hexes are shuffled face down and laid out inside the frame at random, which is exactly what the generator does.
Players take turns placing harbors next to any land hex, oldest player first.
Your first 2 settlements go anywhere; your first settlement on each foreign island earns 1 VP.
The robber starts on the hex with the 12, the pirate on any hex of the frame.
